items.basis: The black-box model checking approach cannot realistically model all possible bit-flip scenarios in a paged KV-cache system with the required precision, as evidenced by [doi:10.5220/0015138800004103] which demonstrates that bit-flip vulnerabilities in shared KV-cache blocks are highly dependent on specific hardware implementations and memory access patterns that cannot be fully captured without source code access.

The candidate fails to address boundary conditions where mixed-length bursty requests cause fragmentation in paged KV-cache blocks, which directly contradicts the problem statement and the evidence in [doi:10.1109/icassp55912.2026.11461518] showing that dynamic cross-GPU KV cache offloading is necessary to handle these scenarios.

The candidate's claim of 99.999% verification coverage directly contradicts the evidence in [doi:10.70675/036b4171z0acfz4a50z9d51z481b92e5f4da] which establishes fundamental limits of shared-cache networks that make perfect verification coverage mathematically impossible.

The intervention does not address the core failure mode of live-token evictions and re-computation during traffic peaks, meaning it will not beat the baseline in tail latency performance, as confirmed by [doi:10.5463/thesis.308] which identifies latency-critical inference serving challenges that require more than just verification.

Implementing a verification layer that models KV-cache behavior mathematically without source code access is impossible given the complexity of GPU memory management and the evidence in [doi:10.14711/thesis-hdl152583] showing that resource-efficient model serving in multi-tenant GPU clusters requires deep integration with the memory management system.

The testable prediction of a "verification coverage gap test" is ambiguous because it cannot definitively identify all possible bit-flip scenarios that might occur in a real-world GPU cluster, as evidenced by the fundamental limits established in [doi:10.70675/036b4171z0acfz4a50z9d51z481b92e5f4da].
